descriptionChirho: Adjective describing a state of preparedness or readiness, used predicatively and attributively across various cases and genders. Multilingual evidence shows consistent adjectival usage: Spanish 'preparados/preparado', Hindi 'तैयार' (taiyaar), Arabic 'مُستَعِدّينَ/مُسْتَعِدُّونَ' (musta'iddīn), Korean '준비된' (junbi-doen = prepared), Swahili 'tayari' (ready). All inflectional variants (NNP, NMS, NMP, NFP, ANS, AFS, ANP) express the same core adjectival concept of being in a state of readiness for action or an event.

Substantivized use of the adjective functioning as an abstract noun meaning 'readiness' or 'preparedness', appearing in the dative singular (DNS). Multilingual evidence confirms the nominal shift: Spanish 'preparación' (preparation, noun), Hindi 'तैयारी' (taiyaarī, noun form with -ī suffix), Arabic 'استِعدادٍ' (isti'dādin, verbal noun/masdar), Korean '준비된' (junbi-doen), Swahili 'utayari' (u- noun class prefix indicating abstract noun). The morphological shift to a noun is clearly attested across translation traditions.
